quote: You talk so fast. I can't understand you.
stewart_read: Customer explicitly signals a pace mismatch in the first 30 seconds. The rep does slow down briefly ('Here. I'll speak a little slower.') but reverts to a fast, run-on delivery style for the rest of the call, visible in the transcript's frequent trailing/restart phrasing.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep on sustained pace control, not just a one-line acknowledgment — the fast, meandering phrasing pattern ('let's see... let's see...') persists through the roof discussion and likely compounded the customer's difficulty following the DQ reasoning.

quote: there are a lot of trees surrounding the area. Right?
stewart_read: The rep jumps directly from address verification to a DQ signal within 90 seconds, skipping the interest and bill-pain Verify items entirely. There was no rapport or curiosity-building before the negative news landed.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: since the imagery clearly showed heavy tree cover, the rep may have judged it more honest to flag the issue immediately rather than build false rapport toward an appointment that would DQ anyway. This is plausible but not clearly the stronger read — even a fast DQ benefits from first anchoring why the customer called.
coaching_implication: Even on a likely-DQ call, run the interest question first — it takes 15 seconds and either surfaces something (roof replacement plans, new tree removal) that changes the qualification, or it closes the call with the customer feeling heard rather than immediately shut down.

quote: Well, I have, sun all morning on the front of my house and all afternoon on the back.
stewart_read: The customer offers a specific, credible counter-fact (front/back sun exposure) that directly challenges a satellite-only read. The rep's response ('Mhmm... but just with how many trees there are') does not probe which side of the house faces south or ask any clarifying question that could actually change the qualification call.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is best supported here — there's no schema-defined DQ override for a customer-reported sun exposure claim, so the rep may have had no procedural path to reopen the DQ even if she wanted to. This is flagged as a schema gap rather than a clean rep failure.
coaching_implication: Flag to Kenny: the schema's dq_rules has no shading-specific override protocol (roof_too_old_no_replacement is about roof age, not tree shading — not a true analog). Ion needs a defined path for when a customer disputes a satellite-based shading DQ with specific sun-exposure claims — does the rep escalate to a site visit, or is satellite imagery final?

quote: I'm gonna ask someone else their opinion, and we shall see. Wait. Just give me a second.
stewart_read: The rep places the customer on hold for roughly a minute to consult a supervisor on a shading-based qualification question. This could be a legitimate escalation for a genuinely borderline case, though the hold is unexplained to the customer beforehand and she is left without any indication of what's being checked or why.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: consulting a supervisor before delivering a final DQ is procedurally sound and better than the rep guessing alone — this may reflect appropriate escalation discipline rather than a knowledge gap.
coaching_implication: If this hold-and-consult is standard practice for ambiguous shading calls, coach the rep to narrate it clearly to the customer up front ('Let me check with my team on your specific sun exposure — one moment') so the pause doesn't feel like confusion or stalling.

quote: I guess what I have to have is somebody who's willing to actually look at what's on I get, know what that is.
stewart_read: The customer is asking, in plain language, for someone to physically assess her property rather than rely on satellite imagery. This is the second time she raises this ask. No specialist site-visit or reassessment path is offered.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is stronger — there's no schema-documented process for offering a physical site assessment on a satellite-based DQ, so this may be a genuine capability gap on Ion's side rather than a rep-level miss.
coaching_implication: Ask Kenny whether Ion has any in-person shading assessment option for borderline satellite DQs; if yes, the rep should know and offer it; if no, this is a product-gap worth surfacing rather than a rep coaching point.

quote: Right? Yeah. The the trees are on the South Side.
schema_reference: qualifiers.credit_qualifier (analog: technical explanation delivered under uncertainty)
stewart_read: The rep's explanation of south/east/west panel placement is delivered with heavy verbal hedging and self-correction ('let's see... south facing roofs, east or west, not as not as much the east and west, but south facing roof') — this is a softener_overuse pattern that undercuts the technical credibility of the explanation right when precision would help the customer trust the verdict.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to pre-script a clean one-line explanation of why south-facing shading matters more than north/west shading, so this lands as confident expertise rather than a rep thinking out loud.
